metadata.title: Electronic (OSCAL) Version of NIST Special Publication 800-53 Revision 5.2.0 MODERATE IMPACT BASELINE to Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations

provenance.mapping-description: Mapping collection from Electronic (OSCAL) Version of NIST Special Publication 800-53 Revision 5.2.0 MODERATE IMPACT BASELINE to Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-1 develops, disseminates, and reviews the access control policy and procedures — one of the family-specific -01 policies the target aggregates. | AU-1 develops/reviews the audit and accountability policy and procedures — a per-family -01 policy in the target's list. | CA-1 develops/reviews assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures — one of the family-specific -01 policies aggregated by the target. | CM-1 develops/reviews the configuration management policy and procedures — a family-specific -01 policy in the target's list. | IA-1 develops/reviews the identification and authentication policy and procedures — the same -01 policy pattern collectively required by the target. | IR-1 develops/reviews the incident response policy and procedures — a family-specific policy the target explicitly aggregates. | PL-1 develops/reviews the planning policy and procedures — an explicit -01 policy the target aggregates. | PS-1 develops/reviews the personnel security policy and procedures — exactly the -01 policy pattern the target aggregates across all families. | RA-1 develops and reviews the risk assessment policy and procedures — a per-family policy of the type the target aggregates. | SA-1 develops/reviews the system and services acquisition policy and procedures — an explicit -01 policy the target aggregates. | SC-1 develops/disseminates system and communications protection policy and procedures — a per-family instance of the target's cross-family requirement. | SI-1 develops/reviews the system and information integrity policy and procedures — a family-specific policy instance of the target's aggregate requirement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-2(1) automated create/enable/modify/disable/remove and account-manager notifications directly automate the account lifecycle and notifications in 800-171 items b and g. | AC-2(4) automatic auditing of account creation, modification, disable and removal directly supports 800-171 item e monitoring of account use and account lifecycle. | AC-6(5) restricting privileged accounts to specific roles supports 800-171 items c and d on specifying account privileges and authorized users. | PS-4 disabling system access upon termination directly implements 800-171 item g.2 notifying and revoking access when users are terminated. | PS-5 modifying access authorization on personnel transfer directly implements 800-171 item g.3 notifying when system usage or need-to-know changes.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-2(13) disabling accounts of high-risk individuals directly implements 800-171 item f.5 on disabling accounts when significant individual risks are discovered. | AC-2(3) disable expired, inactive, unassociated, or policy-violating accounts directly implements 800-171 item f enumeration of when to disable accounts.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-12 selects and generates records for the event types defined per event logging selection, directly implementing the logging capability. | Auditing account creation/modification/removal is a concrete event type contributing to the logging selection required by 03.03.01. | Logging execution of privileged functions is an explicit example event type cited in the 800-171 discussion for what to log.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-3 and 03.01.02 both enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information/CUI and system resources per applicable access control policies — near-identical text.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-4 and 03.01.03 both enforce approved authorizations for information flow within a system and between connected systems — virtually identical requirement statements and discussion.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-5 and 03.01.04 both require identifying duties for separation and defining system access authorizations to support separation of duties — near-identical.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-6 and 03.01.05 item a both employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses necessary to accomplish organizational tasks — near-identical text.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-6 least-privilege base control encompasses restricting privileged access and use of non-privileged accounts as required by 03-01-06.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-6 least-privilege base subsumes preventing non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-6(1) authorizes access to specified security functions and security-relevant information — directly implements 03.01.05 item b. | AC-6(7) periodically reviews assigned privileges and reassigns/removes them as necessary — directly implements 03.01.05 items c and d. | AU-9(4) restricting audit-logging management to a subset of privileged users is a direct application of least privilege to security functions per 03.01.05 item b.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Authorizing access to security functions (configuring access authorizations, audit settings) restricts who can change security-relevant components.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-6(10) preventing non-privileged users from executing privileged functions directly enforces the least-privilege authorization boundary defined in 03.01.05. | AC-6(2) requiring non-privileged accounts for nonsecurity functions directly implements the least-privilege principle articulated in 03.01.05. | AC-6(5) restricting privileged accounts to specific personnel/roles is a direct application of the least-privilege principle in 03.01.05.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-6(2) requires users with privileged accounts to use non-privileged accounts for nonsecurity functions, matching 03-01-06 part b. | AC-6(5) 'Restrict privileged accounts on the system to [personnel/roles]' is textually identical to 800-171 03-01-06 part a.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Restricting privileged accounts to specific personnel prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-6(10) 'Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions' matches 03-01-07 part a verbatim. | AC-6(9) 'Log the execution of privileged functions' is textually identical to 03-01-07 part b.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Preventing non-privileged users from executing privileged functions reinforces the restriction of privileged accounts to authorized personnel.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-7 'Enforce a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts...automatically [action]' is textually identical to 03-01-08.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-8 mandates displaying a system-use notification with privacy/security notices before granting access, covering 03-01-09 and adding acknowledgment and public-system provisions.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-11 device lock text matches 03-01-10 parts a and b nearly verbatim, including retention until re-authentication. | AC-11(1) 'Conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible...with a publicly viewable image' is verbatim 03-01-10 part c.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-12 is the named source control; both require automatic termination of user logical sessions after organization-defined trigger events.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-17 is the named source control; both establish usage restrictions and authorize each type of remote access prior to connection (items a and b). | AC-17(3) requires routing remote access through authorized/managed access control points—exactly matching item c of the target. | AC-17(4) is a named source control; directly implements item d—authorizing remote execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-17(1) mandates automated monitoring and control of remote access methods, directly supporting the target's monitoring/enforcement of remote access policies.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-17(1) monitors and controls remote access methods to detect attacks—a specific instance of 03.14.06's system-monitoring for unauthorized connections. | AU-6 audit record review analyzes logged system events for inappropriate/unusual activity, the same observation-of-events approach cited in 03.14.06 discussion. | SC-7 boundary protection monitors and controls communications at managed interfaces—the external monitoring vantage point 03.14.06 describes. | SI-4(2) provides automated real-time analysis of events—one of the audit-monitoring-software tools 03.14.06 lists for its monitoring capability. | SI-4(4) directly requires monitoring inbound/outbound communications traffic for unusual activity, matching 03.14.06.c verbatim. | SI-4(5) alerts on system-generated indications of compromise from IDS/firewall/audit sources—the alerting output of the monitoring 03.14.06 requires.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-17(2) implements cryptographic mechanisms (VPN/TLS) to protect confidentiality of remote-access sessions—a specific case of transmission encryption. | CP-9(8) requires cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of backup information at rest—same crypto-at-rest mechanism applied to a specific dataset. | SC-28 protects the confidentiality of information at rest, covering the storage half of 03.13.08's transmission-and-storage encryption requirement. | SC-8 protects confidentiality of transmitted information across internal/external networks—the transmission half of 03.13.08.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-18 establishes configuration/connection requirements and authorizes each wireless access, mirroring 03.01.16.a and 03.01.16.b. | AC-18(01) requires protecting wireless access using authentication and encryption—verbatim the same requirement as 03.01.16.d. | AC-18(03) disables embedded wireless capabilities prior to issuance/deployment, identical to 03.01.16.c.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-18(1) mandates authentication of wireless-network users and devices, which is a specific case of the target's device authentication before connection. | IA-4 identifier management explicitly covers device identifiers (MAC, IP, unique tokens) that enable the device identification the target requires. | IA-5(2) PKI/public-key authentication is explicitly cited by the target as a device authentication solution (certificate exchange and revocation checking).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-19 governs mobile device connection authorization; mobile devices are a primary vector of wireless access noted in 03.01.16 discussion. | IA-3 uniquely identifies/authenticates devices before connection—supports the wireless authentication requirement in 03.01.16.d.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-19 establishes configuration/connection requirements and authorizes mobile device connections—directly mirrors 03.01.18.a-b almost verbatim.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-19 governs mobile-device configuration and connection when outside controlled areas — directly overlaps with the travel-to-high-risk-area scenario.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-20 authorizes or prohibits use of external systems for access/processing of organizational information—directly parallels 03.01.20.a and c. | AC-20(01) requires verification of controls or connection agreements before external system use—verbatim the requirement in 03.01.20.c.1-2. | AC-20(02) restricts organization-controlled portable storage devices on external systems—directly mirrors 03.01.20.d.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-20(2) restricts use of organization-controlled portable storage on external systems, directly overlapping with the target's control over portable/removable media use.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AC-22 and 03.01.22 both train authorized individuals and review publicly accessible systems to ensure nonpublic information/CUI is not posted and remove it if discovered.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AT-2 and 03.02.01 both mandate literacy training for users initially and periodically, updating content after events, using the same awareness techniques.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AT-2(2) provides insider threat literacy training, which is one specific topic (insider threat indicators) explicitly required by 03.02.01. | AT-2(3) covers social engineering and social mining recognition training, one of the specific topics mandated by 03.02.01.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AT-3 and 03.02.02 both require role-based training before access/duties, periodically thereafter, on system changes, with content updates after events.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both specify event types selected for logging within the system and require periodic review/update of the selection.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-2 defines the event type selection referenced by 03.03.03.a as the basis for record generation. | AU-3 defines the content that generated audit records must include, directly supporting 03.03.03.a.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-3 lists identical required fields: what/when/where/source/outcome/identity of individuals or objects for audit records.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-12 mandates that generated records include the audit record content defined in AU-3, directly enabling 03.03.02 content. | AU-3(1) covers 03.03.02.b by providing additional audit record information beyond the base content fields.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-5 requires alerting personnel within a defined time and taking additional actions on audit logging process failures, identical to 03.03.04.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-6 explicitly covers review and analysis of physical access logs and reporting findings, matching the target's log-review requirement. | PE-6(1) specifies intrusion alarms and video surveillance as the mechanism to monitor physical access, directly implementing the target's monitoring requirement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-6 requires review/analysis of audit records for inappropriate activity and reporting findings, matching 03.03.05.a and .b. | AU-6(3) has identical wording to 03.03.05.c: analyze and correlate audit records across repositories for organization-wide situational awareness.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-6 requires review, analysis, and reporting of audit records — the very activities the target's reduction/report capability is intended to support. | AU-7(1) provides automated processing/sort/search of audit records, directly implementing the reduction and reporting capability the target requires. | Automated integration of audit review/analysis/reporting processes underlies the report generation and after-the-fact investigation workflows the target requires. | Correlating audit records across repositories is a form of audit record reduction/analysis producing organization-wide reports referenced by the target.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Audit record reduction and report generation directly supports the review, analysis, and reporting required by 03.03.05. | Automated integration of audit review, analysis and reporting processes implements the review/report activities required by 03.03.05.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate an audit record reduction and report generation capability supporting review, analysis, reporting, and after-the-fact incident investigations while preserving original content/time ordering.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require internal system clocks generating time stamps at defined granularity using UTC or a fixed offset — text is nearly identical.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-9(4) authorizes access to management of audit logging functionality to only a subset of privileged users — matches target part b verbatim. | Both mandate protecting audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion using nearly identical wording.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-11 retains audit records to meet regulatory/organizational retention requirements — a specific slice of the target's broader CUI retention mandate.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: AU-11 requires retention of audit records for a defined period, matching 03.03.03.b retention requirement. | AU-12 mandates generation of audit records for the AU-2 event types with AU-3 content, matching 03.03.03.a directly.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require assessing controls in the system and its environment to determine whether security requirements are implemented correctly and producing the desired outcome.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CA-3 information exchange agreements between systems implement the inter-system CUI transfer agreements called out by 03.01.03 (see 03.12.05 reference). | SC-7(4) managed interfaces and traffic flow policy for external telecommunications directly implement the boundary flow-enforcement mechanisms cited in 03.01.03.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate approving/managing information exchange between systems, documenting interface characteristics and responsibilities in exchange agreements, and reviewing/updating those agreements.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CA-3 requires exchange agreements documenting interface characteristics and security requirements between systems—implements the connection/processing agreements in 03.01.20.c.2. | SA-9 requires external service providers to comply with security requirements, matching 03.01.20.b's assignment of security requirements for external systems.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: POAM captures the risk-response decisions where mitigation cannot be completed immediately, as explicitly noted in the 03.11.04 discussion.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require developing/updating a POAM to document planned remediation of weaknesses from assessments, audits, and continuous monitoring.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Continuous monitoring includes ongoing control assessments per the defined frequency, directly overlapping with the periodic assessment mandate of 03.12.01.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require developing and implementing a system-level continuous monitoring strategy that includes ongoing monitoring and security assessments.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Risk monitoring is defined as an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy, directly overlapping with the 03.12.03 requirement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require developing/maintaining a current baseline configuration under configuration control and reviewing/updating it periodically and when components are installed or upgraded.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Baseline configuration under configuration control includes the documented configuration settings the target requires to be established. | CM plan governs configuration item identification and management, which encompasses establishing restrictive configuration settings.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Automated mechanisms maintaining currency/accuracy of the baseline configuration directly implement the target's requirement to keep the baseline current. | CM-6 states 'established settings become part of the configuration baseline' — configuration settings are integral content of the baseline the target maintains. | Configuration change control governs the review/approval of changes to the baseline configuration the target requires to be maintained under config control. | Retaining previous versions of baseline configurations supports the target's ongoing maintenance and update of the current baseline. | The configuration management plan describes how baselines are updated and configuration items managed — directly supporting the target's baseline maintenance requirement. | The system component inventory documents information about system components that the target's baseline explicitly includes.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-2(07) configures notebooks/devices for high-risk travel—an implementation of mobile device configuration/usage restrictions per 03.01.18.a.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate issuing configured systems to individuals traveling to high-risk areas and applying controls upon their return — near-identical requirements.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both define configuration-controlled change types, review/approve with security consideration, implement, and monitor — nearly identical requirements.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-3 requires approving changes with explicit consideration for security impact analyses, which is impact analysis in change context. | Testing and validating changes before finalization is a mechanism to verify security requirements continue to be met post-change. | Verifying impacted controls after changes directly matches target part (b) — confirming security requirements remain satisfied after implementation.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM plan defines processes for identifying configuration items and managing their configuration — the framework in which change control operates. | Developer CM manages/controls integrity of changes and implements only organization-approved changes — parallels target's approve/implement steps. | Requiring security representatives in the change-control body directly supports the review/approve step for configuration-controlled changes. | Testing/validating/documenting changes before finalizing implementation is a core sub-activity of configuration change control. | Verifying controls after changes supports monitoring/review of activities associated with configuration-controlled changes.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require analyzing system changes to determine security impacts prior to implementation — near-identical requirement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-5 enforcing logical access restrictions for system changes is a specialized application of the access-enforcement mechanism required by 03.01.02.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require defining, documenting, approving, and enforcing physical and logical access restrictions associated with system changes — identical wording.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate establishing/documenting configuration settings in the most restrictive mode and approving deviations — near-identical wording.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require configuring the system for only essential capabilities and prohibiting/restricting specified functions, ports, protocols, and services.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Periodic review to identify unnecessary/nonsecure functions/ports/protocols/services and disable/remove them directly matches target parts (c) and (d). | Requiring developers to identify functions, ports, protocols, and services intended for use supports deciding which to restrict for least functionality.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-11 governs user software installation policies and enforcement, overlapping with 03.04.08's deny-all/allow-by-exception authorized software policy. | CM-7(2) prevents program execution per defined policy, directly supporting 03.04.08's deny-all execution enforcement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-7(5) is virtually identical: identify authorized software, employ deny-all/permit-by-exception, and review/update the authorized list.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-8 requires developing/documenting and reviewing/updating a system component inventory — the same core requirement as 03.04.10. | CM-8(1) requires updating the component inventory during installations, removals, and system updates — matches 03.04.10(c) verbatim.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-12 requires identifying/documenting information location and the system components on which information is processed and stored — matches 03.04.11 directly.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CM-12(1) uses automated tools to identify information location on system components, directly supporting 03.04.11's location identification.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CP-9 requires protecting the confidentiality of backup information, directly satisfying target part (a) though not specifying crypto. | SC-28(1) mandates cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of information at rest, covering CUI in backup storage locations.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CP-9(8) implements cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of backup information — the exact requirement of 03.08.09.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: CP-9.8 implements cryptographic mechanisms to protect backup confidentiality — a specific application of the cryptographic protection required by 03.13.11. | SC-28.1 implements cryptographic mechanisms for information at rest — a direct application of 03.13.11's cryptographic CUI protection. | SC-8.1 implements cryptographic mechanisms during transmission to protect confidentiality, a direct application of 03.13.11's cryptographic CUI protection.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-2 uniquely identifies organizational users and associates identification with processes — overlaps with target's identifier assignment to individuals.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-2 mandates uniquely identifying/authenticating organizational users and associating identity with processes acting on their behalf — nearly identical wording.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-2(1) mandates MFA for privileged accounts — the other half of the target's combined privileged-plus-non-privileged MFA requirement. | IA-2(2) mandates MFA for non-privileged accounts — exactly half of the target's requirement (which also covers privileged accounts).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-2(8) implements replay-resistant authentication mechanisms, directly satisfying 03.07.05 part b requirement for replay resistance in nonlocal sessions. | MA-2 approves and monitors maintenance activities whether performed on-site or remotely, directly overlapping 03.07.05 nonlocal maintenance approval. | MA-5 authorizes maintenance personnel including those performing nonlocal maintenance, supporting the approval requirement in 03.07.05 part a.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate replay-resistant authentication mechanisms using nonces or time-synchronous/challenge-response techniques — near-identical language.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require uniquely identifying and authenticating organization-defined devices before establishing a connection — the target's discussion text is drawn directly from IA-3.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require receiving authorization, selecting/assigning individual/group/role/service/device identifiers, and preventing identifier reuse.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-4 identifier management (assigning individual identifiers, usernames) directly supports unique user identification required by the target. | IA-5 manages the authenticators (passwords, biometrics, certificates) that the target uses to authenticate user identities. | IA-8 requires unique identification and authentication of non-organizational users, complementing the target's coverage of 'system users' broadly.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-4(4) directly matches target part (d): managing identifiers by uniquely identifying individuals by status (contractors, foreign nationals).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-5 authenticator management encompasses password-based authenticators including strength, initial content, and change/refresh — superset of target's password requirements.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require verifying recipient identity, establishing initial content, administrative procedures for distribution/loss/revocation, changing defaults, and protecting authenticators.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IA-5(1) mirrors target verbatim: maintain compromised-password list, verify on create/update, transmit only over crypto channels, store cryptographically protected.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure/modification; IA-5(6) refines the target's item (f). | Password-based authenticator management (composition, transmission, storage protection) is a specific instance of the target's authenticator-management lifecycle.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate obscuring authentication feedback during the authentication process to prevent unauthorized exploitation (shoulder surfing) — near-identical wording.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate role-based incident response training within a defined period, upon system changes, and on a defined recurring frequency, with content review/update.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate testing effectiveness of the incident response capability using checklists, walk-throughs, tabletop exercises, and simulations.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IR-3(2) requires coordinating incident response testing with related plans, a specific facet of the target's IR testing requirement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate an incident-handling capability with preparation, detection/analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery consistent with the IR plan.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Automated reporting of incidents is a mechanism implementing the target's incident-reporting requirements (b) and (c). | Automation for availability of IR information/support directly implements item (d) providing advice and assistance to users. | Incident-handling capability underpins tracking, documenting, reporting and providing assistance for incidents required by the target.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Automated support for the incident-handling process is a mechanism implementing the target's incident-handling capability. | The incident response plan defines the capability structure that the target's incident-handling capability must be consistent with. | Tracking/documenting incidents supports the detection/analysis phase of the target's incident-handling capability.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IR-5 exactly matches item (a): 'track and document incidents' with the same discussion about forensics records and information sources. | IR-6 matches items (b) and (c): reporting suspected incidents to the IR capability within a defined period and reporting incident information to defined authorities. | IR-7 matches item (d): providing an incident response support resource offering advice and assistance to users on handling and reporting incidents.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: IR-8 covers every target element (roadmap, structure, reportable incidents, information sharing, responsibilities, distribution, updates, protection) plus additional metrics and approval steps.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MA-3 'Maintenance Tools' matches 03.07.04 part a — approve, control, monitor system maintenance tools plus periodic review. | MA-3(2) 'Inspect Media' checks media containing diagnostic/test programs for malicious code — identical to 03.07.04 part b.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MA-3(1) inspects maintenance tools for improper/unauthorized modifications, supporting the tool-control mechanism required by 03.07.04.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Checking maintenance media for malicious code before use in the system is a direct instance of malicious code detection at an entry point. | Spam protection at system entry/exit points with configuration-management-aligned updates uses the same mechanism model as malicious code protection for unsolicited/malicious content.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MA-3(3) explicitly requires 'Sanitizing or destroying the equipment' to prevent removal of organizational information — same sanitization mechanism as 03.08.03. | SR-12 mandates disposal of components using defined techniques, overlapping with sanitizing CUI-bearing media (scanners, printers, drives) prior to disposal.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MA-4 'Nonlocal Maintenance' directly matches 03.07.05: approve/monitor nonlocal maintenance, strong authentication, terminate sessions when complete.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MA-5 'Maintenance Personnel' matches 03.07.06 verbatim — authorize personnel, list, verify non-escorted access, designate supervisors.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-2 restricts access to system media, providing the access-control component of physical control required in 03.08.01. | MP-5 media transport protects/controls system media outside controlled areas, extending physical control required by 03.08.01. | MP-6 media sanitization prevents disclosure of information from media — directly cited in 03.08.01 discussion as part of secure media handling.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-2 'Restrict access to [media] to [authorized personnel]' is the direct source control for 03.08.02's requirement to restrict CUI media access to authorized personnel or roles.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-3 'Mark system media indicating distribution limitations, handling caveats, and applicable security markings' matches 03.08.04 verbatim in intent and content.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-4 'Media Storage' matches 03.08.01 verbatim — physically control and securely store system media.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-4 'physically control and securely store' media directly implements the physical control mechanism target discussion cites for restricting media access.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-5 'Protect and control media during transport outside of controlled areas; maintain accountability; document activities' matches 03.08.05 (a)(b)(c) directly.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-6 'Sanitize [media] prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or release for reuse' is virtually identical wording to 03.08.03.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: MP-7 and 03.08.07 both restrict/prohibit use of specified media types and prohibit portable/removable storage without an identifiable owner.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PE-2 and 03.10.01 use nearly identical wording: maintain access list, issue credentials, review list, remove when access no longer required.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PE-2 maintains authorized-access lists and credentials that support verifying individual physical access authorizations before granting facility access. | PE-5 controls physical access to output devices (printers, monitors, copiers) to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining output, mirroring target part (e). | PE-6 monitors physical access and reviews access logs, directly supporting the target's audit-log and access-monitoring aspects.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PE-3 enforces the physical access authorizations from the target's access list by verifying authorizations before granting facility ingress.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both enforce physical access authorizations at facility entry/exit, maintain access logs, escort visitors, and secure keys and combinations.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both controls control physical access to system distribution and transmission lines within organizational facilities, using identical examples (locked wiring closets, conduit, sensors).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PE-6 and 03.10.02 use nearly identical wording: monitor physical access to detect/respond to incidents, review logs periodically and upon events.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both title-matched controls require determining alternate work sites for employees and employing security controls/requirements at those sites.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PL-2 develops system security plans covering constituent components, operational context, roles, information types, and safeguards — matches the target's SSP requirement point for point.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PL-4 establishes rules of behavior, receives documented acknowledgment before granting access, and reviews/updates them — mirrors the target's four requirements.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PL-4(1) adds social-media/external-site restrictions into the rules of behavior — a specific extension of the target's RoB content.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PL-4(1) restricts posting organizational information on public websites, directly supporting the goal of preventing CUI on publicly accessible systems.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PL-8 documents security architectures describing safeguards and operational context — content that SSPs reference or incorporate. | RA-2 documents the security categorization results in the security plan — a specific input to the SSP the target requires.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PL-8 develops security architectures as a foundation for system design — the target explicitly cites establishing security architectures as an engineering principle. | SA-3 integrates security considerations across the SDLC — the target explicitly lists incorporating security requirements into the SDLC as an engineering principle.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PS-2 establishes screening criteria for positions and risk designations that directly drive the screening/rescreening activities in the target.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PS-3 requires screening individuals prior to authorizing system access and rescreening per defined conditions — identical to 03.09.01.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PS-4 covers disabling access, revoking authenticators, retrieving property upon termination — all elements of target part (a) plus additional exit-interview requirements. | PS-5 requires reviewing/confirming access authorizations and modifying them on personnel transfer — matching target part (b).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: PS-6 access agreements are signed by individuals before access — the discussion explicitly calls RoB a type of access agreement for system users.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: External personnel security requires providers to comply with organizational policies and monitors compliance, mirroring external-service-provider oversight.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both conduct risk assessments identifying threats/vulnerabilities, likelihood/impact of unauthorized disclosure, and require periodic updates.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: RA-3(1) assesses supply chain risks and requires updates, directly addressing target's explicit inclusion of supply chain risk in the CUI risk assessment. | SR-2 develops a supply chain risk management plan for systems/components/services, addressing target's supply-chain risk assessment scope. | SR-6 assesses supply-chain risks associated with suppliers/contractors and the system/component/service they provide — the exact scope cited in target references.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Acquisition strategies/tools are among the SCRM response actions the plan must document across acquisition and delivery. | SCRM policy and procedures establish the governance basis under which the SCRM plan is developed and maintained. | SCRM team is the coordinated cross-organization body that implements and monitors the SCRM plan. | Supply chain controls/processes to address weaknesses are documented and implemented under the SCRM plan. | Supply chain risk assessment identifies and updates risks (counterfeits, malicious code) that the SCRM plan must document and respond to.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Acquisition process embeds security/privacy requirements into contracts — a primary contract-tool mechanism for supply-chain protection. | Anti-counterfeit policy and procedures are tools/techniques within acquisition strategies protecting against counterfeit-component insertion. | Supplier assessments/reviews inform vetting of contractors — an integral part of acquisition strategies. | Supply chain risk assessment results directly inform which acquisition strategies, tools, and methods are most applicable.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SCRM plan documents the supply-chain processes and controls that implement the required requirements enforcement. | Supply chain risk assessment identifies weaknesses/deficiencies (counterfeits, malicious code) that the requirements process must address.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both monitor and scan systems for vulnerabilities at defined frequencies and when new vulnerabilities emerge, remediate legitimate vulnerabilities, and update scanned vulnerabilities.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Automated flaw remediation status tracking directly supports the flaw identification and update-installation obligations of the target. | Vulnerability monitoring and scanning identifies the flaws that flaw remediation must correct; target discussion explicitly references CVE/CWE-style vulnerability inputs.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: RA-5(2) explicitly updates system vulnerabilities to be scanned at a defined frequency — directly implementing target part (c). | SI-2 identifies, reports, and corrects system flaws and installs security-relevant updates within defined times — directly implements target part (b) remediation. | SI-2(2) uses automated mechanisms to determine whether security-relevant updates are installed on components — supports target's remediation verification.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate responding to findings from security assessments, monitoring, and audits; identical scope with 800-53 adding 'privacy' and 'risk tolerance' qualifiers.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SA-8 applies systems security and privacy engineering principles to specification, design, development, and modification — matches the target verbatim.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require external service providers to comply with security requirements, define roles, and monitor ongoing compliance.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Requires external service providers to identify functions/ports/protocols — a subset of the broader external-services compliance requirement.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate replacing unsupported components and providing alternative sources of continued support; near-identical text.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both control texts are essentially identical—prevent unauthorized/unintended information transfer via shared system resources (object reuse/residual info protection).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-7 and 03.13.01 use nearly identical wording: monitor/control communications at external/internal managed interfaces, implement DMZ subnetworks, connect externally only through managed boundary protection devices.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: External-telecomm managed interfaces establish traffic-flow policy with documented exceptions—operationalizes deny-by-default at the boundary. | SC-7 boundary protection at external/internal managed interfaces provides the enforcement point for the deny-by-default network traffic policy.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-7(3) limits the number of external network connections, a concrete boundary-protection tactic reducing points that must be monitored per 03.13.01. | SC-7(4) specifies managed interfaces and traffic-flow policy for each external telecommunications service, a concrete subset of 03.13.01's managed-interface requirement. | SC-7(5) implements deny-by-default/allow-by-exception traffic policy at managed interfaces, a core boundary-protection behavior of 03.13.01. | SC-7(8) routes traffic through authenticated proxy servers at managed interfaces, a specific boundary-protection implementation of 03.13.01.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate 'deny network communications traffic by default, allow by exception' at system boundary—wording is essentially identical.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-8 protects transmission confidentiality/integrity and expressly cites protected distribution systems (physical/cabling protection) as one implementation, overlapping target scope.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-28(1) requires cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of information at rest—matches the storage-confidentiality portion of 03.13.08. | SC-8(1) mandates cryptographic mechanisms during transmission (TLS/IPsec)—directly matches the transmission-confidentiality portion of 03.13.08.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-10 terminates network connections after inactivity; complements logical session termination and target text explicitly contrasts with 03.13.09 (network disconnect).

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-10 and 03.13.09 both require terminating the network connection at end of session or after a defined inactivity period, with identical de-allocation discussion.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-12 and 03.13.10 both require establishing and managing cryptographic keys per organization-defined key management requirements with identical discussion of manual/automated procedures.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-13 implements cryptography which depends on the key generation/distribution/storage/destruction managed by 03.13.10.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-13 and 03.13.11 both mandate implementing organization-defined types of cryptography to protect information (CUI), with FIPS-validated cryptography recommended.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-15 and 03.13.12 both prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices with defined exceptions and require explicit indication of use to physically present users.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-18 and 03.13.13 both require defining acceptable mobile code/technologies and authorizing, monitoring, and controlling mobile code use.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate 'Protect the authenticity of communications sessions' with near-identical discussion covering man-in-the-middle and session hijacking protection.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SC-28 protection of information at rest via cryptography implements the cryptographic protection mechanism 03.08.05 cites for media during transport.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require identifying, reporting, and correcting system flaws and installing security-relevant software/firmware updates within a defined time period.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both require implementing malicious code protection at entry/exit points, automatic updates, periodic and real-time scanning, and blocking/quarantining detected malicious code.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SI-4 'System Monitoring' matches 03.14.06 clause-by-clause: detect attacks, unauthorized connections, unauthorized use, inbound/outbound traffic.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: SI-5 titled 'Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives' directly requires receiving external and generating/disseminating internal alerts, mirroring 03.14.03.a-b.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both mandate managing and retaining information per applicable laws, EOs, directives, regulations, policies, standards, guidelines, and operational requirements — near-identical wording.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both develop, review/update, and protect a supply-chain risk management plan covering the full system life cycle.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both establish processes to identify/address supply-chain weaknesses and employ controls to protect against supply-chain risks.

props.name: mapping-rationale
props.value: Both employ acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to identify, protect against, and mitigate supply chain risks.
